\section*{Question 5}
\begin{itemize}
\item[] Let \(R\) be the shaded region bounded by the graph of \(y=x e^{x^{2}}\), the line \(y=-2 x\), and the vertical line \(x=1\), as shown in the figure above.
\item[(a)] Find the area of \(R\).
\item[(b)] Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression that gives the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is rotated about the horizontal line \(y=-2\).
(c) Write, but do not evaluate, an expression involving one or more integrals that gives the perimeter of \(R\).
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/e49b711f-5e0b-4607-832e-e52ffaddd056-1.jpg?height=404&width=430&top_left_y=402&top_left_x=1500)
\item[(a)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { Area } & =\int_{0}^{1}\left(x e^{x^{2}}-(-2 x)\right) d x \\
& =\left[\frac{1}{2} e^{x^{2}}+x^{2}\right]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\
& =\left(\frac{1}{2} e+1\right)-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{e+1}{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] Volume \(=\pi \int_{0}^{1}\left[\left(x e^{x^{2}}+2\right)^{2}-(-2 x+2)^{2}\right] d x\)
\item[(c)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
& y^{\prime}=\frac{d}{d x}\left(x e^{x^{2}}\right)=e^{x^{2}}+2 x^{2} e^{x^{2}}=e^{x^{2}}\left(1+2 x^{2}\right) \\
& \text { Perimeter }=\sqrt{5}+2+e+\int_{0}^{1} \sqrt{1+\left[e^{x^{2}}\left(1+2 x^{2}\right)\right]^{2}} d x
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { antiderivative } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { limits and constant }\end{array}\right.\)
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: y^{\prime}=e^{x^{2}}\left(1+2 x^{2}\right) \\ 1: \text { integral } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
